topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, introduces the topic of complement, and sets expectations regarding its complexity and lecture format.

topics.label: Foundations and Core Architecture of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental framework of the complement system, detailing its general cascade logic, nomenclature rules, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Complement Activation and Recognition Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the upstream recognition pathways that trigger complement activation and converge on the local deposition of C3b.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector functions through which activated complement eradicates pathogens and promotes immune clearance.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins that prevent activated complement from damaging healthy host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical Presentations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in different complement components lead to distinct clinical presentations and infection risks.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies pathogens use to evade and inhibit the complement system.

topics.label: Lecture Wrap-up and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture on complement and announces the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
